title: Optimal distance oracles that also report paths
formal: Is there a uniform path-reporting distance-oracle construction for every finite simple undirected graph on \(n\ge2\) vertices with positive real edge weights and every integer \(2\le k\le n\), using at most \(Cn^{1+1/k}\) storage cells, that answers a connected-pair query \((u,v)\) with an estimate \(D\) in at most \(C\) operations and then reports a path \(P\) in at most \(C(1+|P|)\) further operations, with \[d_G(u,v)\le w(P)\le D\le(2k-1)d_G(u,v)?\] The constant \(C\) is absolute, independent of \(n,k\), the graph and its weights.
definitions:
The input is an explicit adjacency-list representation; parallel edges and loops are unnecessary. The distance \(d_G(u,v)\) is the minimum sum of edge weights over paths joining the vertices, and is infinity if they lie in different components. The oracle must report disconnection in constant time. For \(u=v\), it returns zero and the empty path. For a connected pair it outputs consecutive original graph edges forming a simple path; \(|P|\) counts edges, and \(w(P)\) is their total weight. An edge of an auxiliary graph is not an output path unless expanded into original edges within the same bound.

The model has random-access cells storing either one exact real weight or a word of \(\Theta(\log n)\) bits sufficient for polynomially many addresses. Basic arithmetic and comparisons on real weights, word arithmetic and bit operations, and memory access cost one operation. No packing infinitely many weights into one real with unit-cost decoding is allowed. The storage bound includes all retained information from the input graph and all tables needed for answering queries. An external, uncharged copy of the graph is unavailable after preprocessing. Output space for the reported list itself is not charged as persistent oracle storage.

Preprocessing may be randomized, with expected polynomial time in \(n\), and must terminate almost surely, returning an oracle correct for all pairs. It is a Las Vegas construction: every returned oracle obeys the size, stretch and query guarantees. Query and reporting bounds are worst-case and deterministic after the structure is built. These machine, preprocessing and error conventions are editorial specifications of the imported question.

The integer \(k\) is an input parameter, not a fixed constant hidden in big-O. A multiplicative factor of \(k\) in space or an overhead of \(\log k\) therefore does not meet the target. Restricting to \(k\le n\) loses no intended large-k regime: a construction at \(k=n\) has linear space and an adequate stretch for larger \(k\).
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked construction and proof of all simultaneous guarantees, or a complete Lean-checked refutation under the stated model. The estimate must be available in constant time before path reporting, and the path must realize its promised upper bound. A distance-only oracle, a larger constant multiplying \(k\) in the stretch, or constants in space and overhead that grow with \(k\) do not answer this question.
context:
Chechik and Zhang distinguish distance estimates from reporting an actual path. Their introduction records optimal space, stretch and constant query time for distance-only oracles, while the classical path-reporting construction carries extra parameter dependence.

Their 2024 result provides linear-size oracles with logarithmic stretch, and more generally improves path-reporting tradeoffs. This motivates closing the remaining gap with the exact 2k−1 stretch and parameter-independent constant overhead selected here.
why: This asks whether compact distance summaries can return actual routes without losing their best size and stretch guarantees.

import_provenance.original_title: Optimal distance oracles that also report paths
import_provenance.original_statement: For undirected positively weighted graphs, can a path-reporting distance oracle simultaneously achieve O(n^(1+1/k)) space, stretch 2k−1, and O(1) query overhead plus time proportional to the reported path? This asks to match Chechik's distance-only bounds while returning an actual approximate shortest path.

context_blocks.text: Chechik and Zhang distinguish distance estimates from reporting an actual path. Their introduction records optimal space, stretch and constant query time for distance-only oracles, while the classical path-reporting construction carries extra parameter dependence.

Their 2024 result provides linear-size oracles with logarithmic stretch, and more generally improves path-reporting tradeoffs. This motivates closing the remaining gap with the exact 2k−1 stretch and parameter-independent constant overhead selected here.

sentences: A compact representation of a weighted graph must answer shortest-path queries approximately.
The requested oracle must produce an actual path as well as a distance estimate.
Space, stretch and query overhead must achieve the stated bounds uniformly in the parameter k.
The source distinguishes the known distance-only tradeoff from stronger path-reporting guarantees.
Resolving the question would determine whether recovering a route inherently costs more than estimating its length.
